q01: "Data Science Fundamentals" is a 6-month course designed for learners with a strong foundation in programming (prerequisite: Python programming skills) and basic statistics. This course covers essential skills and topics in data science, including data wrangling and preprocessing, machine learning algorithms, data visualization using popular libraries such as Matplotlib and Seaborn, and statistical modeling with scikit-learn. Students will also learn to work with popular data science tools like Pandas and NumPy, and develop skills in data storytelling and communication. By the end of this course, learners will be able to design and implement data-driven solutions to real-world problems.
q02: "Machine Learning and Deep Learning with Python: This course is designed for intermediate-level learners with prior programming experience and a basic understanding of linear algebra and calculus. Students will gain hands-on experience in building and deploying machine learning models using popular Python libraries such as TensorFlow and Keras, and will learn to apply deep learning techniques to image and speech recognition, natural language processing, and predictive analytics. The course covers topics including supervised and unsupervised learning, neural networks, convolutional and recurrent neural networks, and model evaluation and optimization, with a target duration of 12 weeks."
q03: "Develop a comprehensive understanding of full-stack web development using Python and JavaScript in this intermediate-level course. Students will learn to design, build, and deploy dynamic web applications, mastering skills in front-end development with JavaScript, back-end development with Python, and database management using popular frameworks such as Flask and Django. Topics covered include HTML/CSS, JavaScript libraries and frameworks like React and Node.js, and Python libraries like SQLAlchemy and Django ORM. This course is designed to be completed in approximately 12 weeks, requiring a strong foundation in programming fundamentals and prior experience with Python and JavaScript."
q04: In this comprehensive course, students will develop advanced skills in cybersecurity, network defense, and ethical hacking, building on a strong foundation in computer systems and networking principles. Prerequisites include a basic understanding of computer systems, networking fundamentals, and programming concepts. Through a combination of lectures, hands-on labs, and real-world case studies, students will learn to identify and mitigate vulnerabilities, design and implement secure network architectures, and employ ethical hacking techniques to test and improve the security of computer systems and networks. This course is designed to be completed in approximately 12 weeks, with a target of 120 hours of instruction.
q05: This course covers the design, implementation, and management of cloud computing infrastructure and DevOps deployment strategies, focusing on scalability, reliability, and security. Prerequisites include a basic understanding of computer systems, networking fundamentals, and programming skills in languages such as Python or Java. Students will learn to deploy and manage cloud-based infrastructure using tools like AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud, and develop skills in continuous integration, continuous deployment, and continuous monitoring using DevOps practices and tools like Jenkins, Docker, and Kubernetes. The target duration of this course is approximately 12 weeks, with a mix of lectures, hands-on labs, and project-based learning.
cs06: "Data Engineering with SQL and Spark" is a 12-week course designed for backend developers looking to transition into data engineering. Prerequisites include a strong foundation in programming, specifically in languages such as Java, Python, or Scala, as well as experience with SQL and data modeling. This course covers the skills and topics necessary to design, develop, and deploy scalable data pipelines using Apache Spark, including data ingestion, processing, and storage, as well as data warehousing and business intelligence with SQL. Students will learn to work with big data frameworks, implement data quality and governance, and develop data engineering best practices.
cs07: "Android Mobile App Development Fundamentals" is a beginner-level course that covers the essential skills and topics required to develop mobile applications for Android devices from scratch. This course is designed for students with no prior programming experience, and it starts with the basics of Java programming, Android Studio, and Android SDK. Students will learn how to design, develop, and deploy Android apps, including user interface design, data storage, networking, and security, as well as how to publish their apps on the Google Play Store. The course is approximately 12 weeks long and includes hands-on projects and assignments to help students build a comprehensive understanding of Android mobile app development.
cs08: "Database Fundamentals and Optimization" is a 6-week course designed for intermediate learners with a background in computer science or a related field. This course covers the essential skills and topics in database management, including relational database design principles, indexing techniques, and query optimization strategies. Students will learn to design efficient database schemas, implement indexing methods, and tune queries for improved performance, as well as understand the trade-offs between data consistency, availability, and scalability. By the end of the course, learners will be able to apply their knowledge to real-world database systems and improve their overall database management skills.
math01: "Calculus Review for Engineering Fundamentals" is a foundational course designed for students entering an engineering degree program, requiring a prerequisite of high school mathematics or equivalent. This 12-week course covers essential skills and topics in differential and integral calculus, including limits, derivatives, applications of derivatives, and basic integration techniques, as well as multivariable calculus and vector calculus. Through a combination of lectures, assignments, and problem-solving exercises, students will develop a strong understanding of calculus concepts and their practical applications in engineering, preparing them for advanced coursework in their chosen field.
math02: This course covers the fundamental concepts of linear algebra and probability, providing a solid foundation for understanding machine learning techniques. Prerequisites include a basic understanding of calculus and programming fundamentals. Students will learn to apply linear algebra skills such as vector operations, matrix decomposition, and eigenvalue analysis, as well as probability concepts including conditional probability, Bayes' theorem, and statistical inference. Upon completion, learners will be able to interpret and analyze machine learning papers, and apply linear algebra and probability principles to real-world problems. The course is designed to be completed in approximately 12 weeks.
math03: "Introduction to Applied Statistics for Research Interpretation" is a 6-week course designed for students with a basic understanding of algebra and prior knowledge of research methods. This course focuses on developing skills in statistical analysis and interpretation, covering topics such as descriptive statistics, probability, hypothesis testing, confidence intervals, and regression analysis. Students will learn to critically evaluate research studies, understand statistical results, and communicate findings effectively, without requiring programming skills. By the end of the course, learners will be able to apply statistical concepts to real-world research scenarios and make informed decisions based on data-driven insights.
math04: "Foundations of Discrete Mathematics and Logic" is a course designed for students with a basic understanding of mathematics and computer science principles, typically at the freshman or sophomore level. This course covers the essential skills and topics in discrete mathematics and logic, including propositional and predicate logic, set theory, graph theory, and combinatorics, as well as mathematical proof techniques and induction. Students will learn to apply these concepts to solve problems in computer science, such as algorithm design, data structures, and computational complexity. The course is expected to last 12-15 weeks, with a total of 45-60 contact hours.
math05: "Mathematics for Differential Equations: Foundations and Applications" is a 12-week course designed for students with a strong background in high school algebra. This course will cover the essential mathematical concepts and skills required for the study of differential equations, including linear algebra, vector calculus, and ordinary differential equations. Students will develop their problem-solving skills in topics such as systems of linear equations, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, and first-order and higher-order differential equations, ultimately preparing them for advanced courses in differential equations and mathematical modeling. Prerequisites include a strong understanding of high school algebra and trigonometry.
biz01: "Financial Accounting Fundamentals" is a 12-week course designed for students with a basic understanding of business principles and prior accounting knowledge. This course covers the essential skills and topics necessary to comprehend a company's annual report, including financial statement analysis, accounting equation, asset valuation, and cash flow management. Students will learn to prepare and interpret balance sheets, income statements, and cash flow statements, as well as understand key financial ratios and metrics. By the end of the course, students will be able to critically evaluate a company's financial performance and make informed decisions.
biz02: "Develop a comprehensive digital marketing and social media strategy for small business owners, this course covers the essential skills and topics necessary to effectively promote and engage with target audiences. Prerequisites include basic computer skills and a fundamental understanding of business operations. Students will learn to create and implement a digital marketing plan, leveraging social media platforms, search engine optimization (SEO), and content marketing to drive website traffic, generate leads, and increase sales. The course targets a duration of 6 weeks, with a focus on hands-on training and real-world applications, and is designed for business owners and marketing professionals looking to enhance their digital marketing skills."
biz03: "Foundations of Entrepreneurship and Fundraising" is a 6-week course designed for beginners, requiring no prior experience. This course covers essential skills and topics, including business planning, market analysis, financial modeling, and pitch development, as well as fundraising strategies and techniques for securing investments. Students will learn how to create a comprehensive business plan, identify target markets, and develop a persuasive pitch to secure funding, ultimately gaining the knowledge and confidence to launch and grow a successful startup.
biz04: This course covers the fundamentals of project management, from planning and execution to monitoring and control, and culminates in the application of agile methodologies for efficient delivery. Prerequisites include a basic understanding of business operations and prior experience with project coordination. Students will develop skills in project scope definition, resource allocation, risk management, and stakeholder communication, as well as learn to apply agile frameworks such as Scrum and Kanban. The course is designed to be completed in approximately 12 weeks, with a mix of lectures, case studies, and group projects.
biz05: "Corporate Finance and Investment Analysis for Banking Professionals" is a 12-week course designed for individuals seeking a career change into the banking industry. This course is open to learners with a bachelor's degree in finance, accounting, or a related field, or those with significant work experience in a related field. Students will develop skills in financial statement analysis, investment valuation, and portfolio management, as well as gain a deep understanding of corporate finance concepts, including capital structure, cost of capital, and dividend policy. By the end of the course, learners will be able to analyze financial statements, evaluate investment opportunities, and make informed decisions in a banking context.
biz06: "Supply Chain and Operations Management for Manufacturing" is a 12-week course designed for individuals with a bachelor's degree in business or a related field, or equivalent work experience. This course covers the essential skills and knowledge required to manage supply chain and operations in a manufacturing setting, including demand planning, inventory management, logistics and transportation, quality control, and process improvement. Students will learn to analyze and optimize supply chain processes, manage global supply chain risks, and implement lean manufacturing principles to enhance efficiency and productivity. By the end of the course, students will be able to develop and implement effective supply chain strategies, manage cross-functional teams, and make data-driven decisions to drive business success.
health01: "Foundations of Nutrition Science" is a 12-week course designed for students with a basic understanding of biology and chemistry. This course will equip learners with the skills to critically evaluate scientific evidence in nutrition and develop a comprehensive understanding of the relationship between diet, health, and disease. Topics covered include macronutrient metabolism, micronutrient functions, and the impact of lifestyle factors on nutritional health, with a focus on evidence-based practice and critical thinking. By the end of the course, students will be able to analyze and apply scientific research to inform their understanding of nutrition and healthy eating.
health02: This course provides a comprehensive introduction to public health and epidemiology fundamentals, tailored for non-clinical professionals. Prerequisites include a basic understanding of health sciences and statistics. Students will develop skills in data analysis, disease surveillance, and outbreak investigation, as well as learn key concepts such as population health, health disparities, and infectious disease transmission. The course covers topics including epidemiological study design, biostatistics, and data visualization, with a target duration of 6 weeks.
health03: This course, "Foundations of Mental Health Support," is designed for support workers with a basic understanding of human services (prerequisite: completion of a human services certificate or equivalent). Over the course of 12 weeks, students will develop essential skills in understanding mental health concepts, including the biological and psychological factors influencing mental well-being, common mental health disorders, and evidence-based interventions. Topics covered will include the principles of trauma-informed care, crisis management, and effective communication strategies for supporting individuals with mental health needs. By the end of the course, students will be able to apply theoretical knowledge to real-world scenarios, promoting a supportive and inclusive environment for individuals with mental health concerns.
health04: "Foundations of Anatomy and Physiology for Nursing" is a foundational course designed for students preparing to enter a nursing program. This course covers the essential principles of human anatomy and physiology, including the structure and function of the body's systems, cells, and tissues, as well as the regulation of various physiological processes. Prerequisites include a high school diploma or equivalent, and a basic understanding of biology and chemistry. Through a combination of lectures, discussions, and interactive activities, students will develop a comprehensive understanding of the human body and its functions, as well as the skills to apply this knowledge in a clinical setting. The course is approximately 12 weeks in duration.
health05: "Global Health Systems and Policy" is a 12-week course that explores the complexities of healthcare delivery and policy-making across diverse cultural and economic contexts. This intermediate-level course (prerequisites: introductory courses in public health, global studies, or a related field) examines the key concepts, theories, and practices shaping global health systems, including health governance, financing, and service delivery. Students will develop skills in analyzing health policy, evaluating global health initiatives, and advocating for health equity, with topics covered including global health frameworks, health systems strengthening, and policy-making for infectious disease control.
comm01: "Effective Public Speaking and Presentation" is a course designed for individuals seeking to develop confidence and skills in presenting to various audiences. Prerequisites include basic communication skills and a high school diploma or equivalent. This 6-week course covers essential topics such as speechwriting, body language, vocal techniques, and presentation design, as well as advanced skills like handling questions and managing stage fright. By the end of the course, students will be able to craft compelling presentations, engage their audience, and deliver confident public speeches.
comm02: This course, "Effective Negotiation and Persuasion for Emerging Leaders," is designed for individuals with a foundational understanding of business principles and practices, typically acquired through completion of a bachelor's degree or equivalent experience. Students will develop essential skills in negotiation and persuasion, including active listening, assertive communication, and strategic planning, to effectively navigate complex business interactions and drive results. Through a combination of lectures, case studies, and interactive exercises, participants will explore topics such as conflict resolution, influence tactics, and stakeholder management, with a focus on building strong relationships and achieving mutually beneficial outcomes. The course is expected to last approximately 6 weeks, with a total of 12-15 hours of instruction.
comm03: "Effective Leadership for Small Technical Teams" is a 6-week course designed for individuals with a strong technical background and a minimum of 2 years of experience in a leadership or management role. This course will equip students with the skills and knowledge necessary to lead and motivate small technical teams, including strategic planning, communication, conflict resolution, and delegation. Students will learn how to set clear goals and expectations, foster a culture of innovation and collaboration, and make informed decisions that drive team success. By the end of the course, students will be able to apply leadership principles to real-world scenarios and develop a personalized leadership plan to achieve their team's objectives.
comm04: "Business Writing and Professional Communication for Non-Native English Speakers" is a course designed for intermediate-level learners (prerequisite: English proficiency at B1 level or higher) who aim to improve their business writing and professional communication skills in English. This 6-week course focuses on developing essential skills in writing business emails, reports, and proposals, as well as delivering effective presentations and engaging in professional conversations. Topics covered include business letter writing, tone and style, grammar and vocabulary for business communication, and cultural nuances in professional communication. By the end of the course, learners will be able to produce clear, concise, and well-structured business writing and communicate confidently in professional settings.
comm05: "Effective Conflict Resolution and Difficult Conversations in the Workplace" is a 3-credit course designed for students at the intermediate level (prerequisite: Business Communication or equivalent). This course focuses on developing essential skills in navigating workplace conflicts and challenging conversations, including active listening, assertive communication, and problem-solving strategies. Students will explore topics such as conflict escalation, de-escalation techniques, and negotiation tactics, as well as strategies for building and maintaining positive working relationships. Upon completion, students will be able to manage conflicts and difficult conversations with confidence and professionalism.
sci01: "Climate Science and Energy Transition: This course explores the fundamental principles of climate science, including atmospheric dynamics, greenhouse gases, and climate modeling. Students will also delve into the energy transition, examining the role of renewable energy sources, energy storage, and grid management in mitigating climate change. Prerequisites include a basic understanding of physics and mathematics, as well as introductory courses in environmental science or sustainability. This 12-week course is designed to equip learners with the knowledge and skills necessary to analyze and address the complex relationships between energy systems, climate change, and sustainable development."
sci02: "Foundations of Physics and Mechanics" is a beginner-level course designed for adult learners returning to study, requiring no prior knowledge of physics. This 12-week course covers the fundamental principles of physics and mechanics, including kinematics, dynamics, energy, and momentum, as well as topics such as Newton's laws, friction, and circular motion. Students will develop skills in problem-solving, mathematical modeling, and critical thinking, with a focus on applying theoretical concepts to real-world scenarios. By the end of the course, learners will be able to analyze and solve physics-related problems, and will have a solid foundation for further study in physics and related fields.
sci03: "Introduction to Molecular Biology and Genetics" is a foundational course that covers the fundamental principles of molecular biology and genetics from the basics. This course is designed for students with a strong background in high school biology and chemistry, and is ideal for those seeking a comprehensive understanding of DNA structure and function, gene expression, genetic variation, and molecular mechanisms of inheritance. Through a combination of lectures, discussions, and hands-on laboratory exercises, students will develop skills in DNA sequencing, PCR, and gene cloning, as well as analyze and interpret genetic data. The course is expected to last 12 weeks, with a total of 48 contact hours, and is suitable for students seeking a solid foundation in molecular biology and genetics.
sci04: "Electrical Engineering Fundamentals: Circuits, Signals, and Electronics" is a foundational course that covers the essential principles and practices of electrical engineering. Prerequisites include a basic understanding of algebra and trigonometry, as well as prior knowledge of physics and mathematics. This 12-week course will equip students with the skills to analyze and design electrical circuits, understand the behavior of electronic signals, and apply fundamental concepts in electronics, including circuit theory, signal processing, and semiconductor devices. By the end of the course, students will be able to apply mathematical models to circuit analysis, design and troubleshoot electronic circuits, and understand the principles of signal processing and transmission.
sci05: This course covers the fundamental principles of organic chemistry, providing a comprehensive foundation for medical school entrance exams. Prerequisites include a strong understanding of general chemistry and algebra, as well as a basic knowledge of biochemistry. Students will develop skills in identifying and synthesizing organic compounds, understanding reaction mechanisms, and applying stereochemistry and spectroscopy concepts. The course targets a duration of 12 weeks, with a focus on in-depth analysis of key topics such as functional groups, aromatic compounds, and organic synthesis, preparing students for the organic chemistry section of the Medical College Admission Test (MCAT).
arts01: "Foundations of Music Theory and Composition" is a course designed for intermediate learners, requiring prior knowledge of music fundamentals. This 12-week course covers essential music theory concepts, including chord progressions, scales, and rhythm, as well as composition techniques, such as melody writing, harmony, and form. Students will develop skills in analyzing and notating music, and learn to apply theoretical knowledge to create original compositions. By the end of the course, learners will be able to read and write music, understand musical structures, and begin composing their own music.
arts02: "Survey of Modern World History: This course explores the major events, themes, and trends of the modern world from the Industrial Revolution to the present day, covering the rise of global empires, two World Wars, the Cold War, decolonization, and contemporary globalization. Prerequisites include a basic understanding of world history and a high school diploma or equivalent. Through lectures, discussions, and readings, students will develop critical thinking and analytical skills to understand the complex interactions between politics, economy, culture, and society in shaping modern world history. The course is designed to be completed in 12 weeks."
arts03: "Explore the fundamental principles of philosophy and develop essential skills in ethical reasoning through this introductory course. Prerequisites include a high school diploma or equivalent, with no prior knowledge of philosophy required. This 6-week course delves into key topics such as metaphysics, epistemology, and ethics, while cultivating critical thinking, argumentation, and problem-solving skills. Students will analyze classic philosophical texts, engage in debates, and apply ethical theories to real-world scenarios, fostering a deeper understanding of the subject and its relevance to everyday life."
arts04: "Develop your creative writing and storytelling skills in this intermediate-level course, ideal for those with prior writing experience. Through a combination of lectures, workshops, and writing exercises, you will learn to craft compelling narratives, develop complex characters, and master the art of pacing and plot structure. Topics covered include character development, setting and world-building, dialogue and voice, and the techniques of suspense and plot twist. This 12-week course is designed to help you produce a short story or novel excerpt, and is suitable for writers of science fiction, fantasy, mystery, and other genres."
arts05: "Introduction to Photography and Visual Design" is a foundational course designed for complete beginners, requiring no prior experience or prerequisites. This 12-week course covers the essential skills and topics in photography and visual design, including camera operation, composition, lighting, color theory, and visual storytelling. Students will learn to capture and edit high-quality images using industry-standard software, and develop a visual design language to effectively communicate their ideas through images. By the end of the course, students will have a solid understanding of the principles of photography and visual design, and be able to apply their skills in a variety of creative contexts.
edu01: "Effective Classroom Teaching Methods" is a foundational course designed for new educators, requiring no prior teaching experience. This 6-week course covers essential skills and topics, including lesson planning, classroom management, differentiated instruction, and assessment strategies. Students will learn how to create engaging learning environments, develop effective communication skills, and cultivate a growth mindset in their students. By the end of the course, participants will be equipped with the knowledge and confidence to implement best practices in their own classrooms.
edu02: In this course, students will develop the skills and knowledge necessary to design and build effective online courses, with a focus on instructional design principles, adult learning theory, and multimedia authoring tools. Prerequisites include a basic understanding of educational technology and prior experience with online learning platforms. Through a combination of lectures, discussions, and hands-on activities, students will learn to create engaging online content, develop assessments and evaluations, and implement interactive elements to enhance learner engagement. The course will cover topics such as learning objectives, course architecture, and accessibility, with a target duration of 6 weeks. By the end of the course, students will be able to design and build a comprehensive online course that meets the needs of diverse learners.
edu03: "Mathematics Education for Primary School Teachers: Effective Strategies and Techniques" is a course designed for educators with a basic understanding of mathematics and teaching principles. This 6-week course will equip participants with the skills and knowledge to create engaging and interactive math lessons for primary school children, covering topics such as number sense, algebraic thinking, and geometric reasoning. Through a combination of lectures, discussions, and hands-on activities, participants will learn how to assess student understanding, differentiate instruction, and foster a growth mindset in their students, ultimately leading to improved math literacy and confidence.
edu04: "Assessment and Evaluation of Student Learning" is a 6-week course designed for graduate-level students, requiring a background in education or a related field. This course focuses on developing skills in designing and implementing effective educational assessments, measuring student learning outcomes, and interpreting data to inform instruction. Topics covered include test theory, validity and reliability, rubric development, and data-driven decision making, as well as the application of various assessment methods, such as formative and summative assessments, and performance tasks. By the end of the course, students will be able to create and implement assessments that align with learning objectives and evaluate student learning in a fair and accurate manner.
law01: "Foundations of Law and Legal Reasoning" is a 6-week course designed for non-lawyers, introducing the fundamental principles of law and legal reasoning. This course assumes no prior knowledge of law and is ideal for individuals seeking to understand the basics of legal systems, including the structure of the judiciary, key legal concepts, and the role of precedent in shaping legal decisions. Through a combination of lectures, discussions, and case studies, students will develop essential skills in legal analysis, critical thinking, and problem-solving, enabling them to navigate complex legal issues and make informed decisions in both personal and professional contexts.
law02: This course explores the fundamental principles and concepts of human rights and international humanitarian law, examining the key international instruments and institutions that govern these areas. Prerequisites include a basic understanding of international law and relations, as well as a strong foundation in critical thinking and analytical skills. Through a combination of lectures, case studies, and group discussions, students will develop the skills to analyze complex human rights and humanitarian law issues, identify relevant international norms and standards, and apply these principles to real-world scenarios. The course is designed to be completed in 12 weeks, with a target of 45 hours of instruction.
law03: "Public Policy Analysis and Governance for a Civil Service Career" is a 12-week course designed for students with a bachelor's degree in a related field or equivalent experience. This course covers the essential skills and knowledge required for a successful civil service career, including policy analysis, governance, and public administration. Students will learn to evaluate policy options, analyze data, and develop effective governance strategies, as well as understand the role of government in addressing social, economic, and environmental issues. By the end of the course, students will be able to apply theoretical concepts to real-world scenarios, think critically about policy decisions, and communicate effectively with stakeholders.
law04: "Explore the principles and practices of sustainability, environmental policy, and corporate responsibility in this comprehensive course. Building on foundational knowledge of business and environmental studies, students will develop skills in environmental impact assessment, stakeholder engagement, and sustainable supply chain management. Topics covered include climate change mitigation and adaptation strategies, green finance, and regulatory frameworks for environmental governance. This 12-week course is designed for upper-level undergraduate students and graduate students, requiring a prerequisite of Environmental Studies 301 or equivalent."
lang01: "English Grammar and Academic Writing for Advanced Learners" is a 12-week course designed for students with a strong foundation in English language skills, typically requiring a B2 level of proficiency or higher. This course focuses on refining advanced grammar structures, including complex sentence formations, conditional tenses, and passive voice, as well as developing effective academic writing skills through the analysis of various essay types, research paper formats, and peer review techniques. Students will learn to articulate complex ideas, organize coherent arguments, and edit their writing for clarity and precision, ultimately enhancing their ability to produce high-quality academic writing.
lang02: "Chinese for Business Travelers: Beginner Level" is a 6-week course designed for individuals with no prior knowledge of the Chinese language. This course covers the essential skills and topics necessary for business travel in China, including basic Chinese characters, pronunciation, and grammar, as well as business-related vocabulary and phrases. Students will learn to communicate effectively in everyday business situations, such as ordering food, making introductions, and negotiating, and will gain a solid foundation in reading, writing, and speaking Chinese. By the end of the course, students will be able to hold basic conversations and understand common business-related expressions in Chinese.
lang03: "Technical Communication in English for Professionals" is a course designed for individuals with intermediate English proficiency (B1-B2 CEFR level) who aim to enhance their professional communication skills in a technical workplace. This course focuses on developing skills in writing, presenting, and communicating complex technical information effectively to diverse audiences, including report writing, proposal development, and presentation techniques. Students will learn to navigate technical vocabulary, understand industry-specific terminology, and apply best practices in technical documentation, with a target duration of 12 weeks.
